newsitem.title: FRANCE: France welcomes Turkey's steps on human rights.
newsitem.headline: France welcomes Turkey's steps on human rights.

text.p: France welcomed on Monday a Turkish pledge to clean up its record on human rights, saying this would help improve Ankara's ties with Europe.
"This is a step in the right direction towards a hoped-for re-establishment of good relations between Turkey and Europe," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
He referred to remarks made by Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller last week in Ankara in which she announced human rights reform measures.
Ciller said Turkey would cut the period of detention in custody and make changes to the State Security Court system, though she gave few details.
Suspects held under anti-terror laws can now be detained for up to a month in 10 emergency rule provinces in the mainly-Kurdish southeast and two weeks in the rest of Turkey.

Ciller, a pro-Western conservative in coalition with Islamists, said Europe would have no reason to shun Turkey once its rights performance improved. "If Europe continues to keep Turkey out it will become a Christian club. That is dangerous for regional and world peace," she said.
Amnesty International launched a worldwide campaign this month to highlight rights abuses in Turkey, including extrajudicial killings, torture and disappearances.

The rights group has criticised Turkey for failing to live up to previous promises to stamp out rights violations. The European Parliament last month threatened to hold back hundreds of millions of dollars in European Union aid to Turkey, partly because of its rights record.
